trees.title: The car won't start
trees.summary: You turn the key or press the start button — and nothing good happens.
trees.safety: Before any check: apply the parking brake, put the gear lever in park (P) or neutral, and never touch moving parts or the ignition system while the engine is running.

n1.q: What happens when you try to start the car?

options.label: Nothing — no sound, and the dashboard lights are weak or off
The engine turns over (a “grr-grr” sound) but doesn't start
The engine starts for a moment and immediately stalls

n2.q: Do the headlights and dashboard lights come on when you switch to the on position?

options.label: Yes, at normal brightness — only the starter doesn't work

n4.q: Is the car automatic? Is the gear lever in P or N? (Manual: is the clutch pedal pressed all the way down?)

options.label: No — it was in gear / the clutch wasn't pressed
Yes, everything is in the right position

n3.q: Is there fuel in the tank, and the fuel gauge isn't on empty?

options.label: The tank is nearly empty or empty

n6.q: Is the key/immobiliser warning light flashing on the dashboard?

n5.q: What type of engine is it?

options.label: Diesel, after the fuel ran out and was refilled

r-battery.result: The battery is weak or flat, or its connections are loose or corroded
r-battery.text: The starter needs a very strong current. A weak battery has enough for the lights but not for the starter — hence the clicking. Common causes: lights left on, an old battery (usually after 3–5 years), only short trips, and cold weather.
actions: Check that the battery terminals are tight and free of white-green corrosion.
Jump-start it with cables from another car in the correct order, or with a portable jump starter.
After starting, drive for at least half an hour so the battery charges, and have the battery and charging system checked at a garage.
If the battery warning light comes on while driving, the problem is probably the charging system (the alternator), not the battery.

r-gear.result: The safety switch is preventing starting in gear
r-gear.text: In an automatic car you can only start in P or N; in most manual cars, only when the clutch pedal is pressed all the way down. This protects against the car lurching forward when it starts.
actions: Move to P (or N) / press the clutch all the way down and try again.
In an automatic car: also press the brake pedal while starting.

r-starter.result: A fault in the starter motor, its relay, or the wiring
r-starter.text: When the electrics are fine but the starter doesn't turn, the problem is usually the starter motor itself, the starter relay, a fuse, or a loose contact.
actions: Check the starter fuse in the owner's manual.
Call for a tow or roadside assistance; this isn't a fault you can fix at the roadside.

r-fuel.result: The car has run out of fuel
r-fuel.text: After refuelling, in a petrol car it's usually enough to turn the key to the on position for a few seconds before starting, so the fuel pump can fill the system.
actions: Fill up with the correct type of fuel.
In a diesel car you may need to bleed air from the fuel system — follow the owner's manual.

r-immobiliser.result: The immobiliser isn't recognising the key
r-immobiliser.text: The immobiliser stops the car starting when it doesn't recognise the chip in the key. A weak key fob battery or a damaged key can cause this.
actions: Try the spare key.
With a start button: hold the fob near the spot the owner's manual specifies (sometimes by the steering column).

r-ignition-fuel.result: A fault in the fuel supply or ignition
r-ignition-fuel.text: The engine needs fuel, air and a spark (in petrol engines) at the right moment. When it turns over but doesn't start, one of these is missing: the fuel pump, a clogged filter, a sensor, the spark plugs, or the ignition coil.
actions: Don't keep trying to start it again and again — this drains the battery and overheats the starter. Try for a few seconds at most, and wait between attempts.
Call roadside assistance or a tow to a garage.

r-idle.result: A fault in idle control or the air/fuel supply
r-idle.text: An engine that starts and immediately stalls may be suffering from a clogged air filter, a faulty sensor, or a throttle problem.
actions: Check whether the “check engine” light is on.
Go to a garage for a computerised diagnosis.

r-glow.result: Weak glow plugs — a cold diesel engine
r-glow.text: A diesel engine ignites from compression heat. In cold weather, the glow plugs warm the combustion chamber before starting.
actions: Switch to the on position and wait for the glow plug light (a yellow coil) to go out — only then start the engine.
If the problem happens every cold morning, have the glow plugs checked at a garage.

r-diesel-air.result: Air has entered the diesel fuel system
r-diesel-air.text: When the diesel fuel runs out, air is drawn into the lines and the pump can't build up pressure.
actions: Many cars have a hand pump or an air-bleeding procedure — follow the owner's manual.
If not, call roadside assistance. For next time: don't drive a diesel car until the tank is empty.
